guidance.title: Account status incorrect (open/closed)
guidance.guidance: Consumer says an account is reported as open when it was closed (or vice versa). Common when a closure request wasn't processed downstream to the bureau feed. Furnisher should confirm current account status and correct the reported status if it's stale.

rationale: Confident classification, low-risk reason code, furnisher in good standing.

guidance.title: Incorrect date opened
guidance.guidance: Consumer disputes the reported account-opening date, which affects how the account factors into credit age. Frequently caused by confusing an account renewal or reissue date with the true origination date. Furnisher should confirm the original opening date from account records.

guidance.title: Duplicate account reported
guidance.guidance: The same underlying account appears more than once on the report, often after a balance transfer, account renumbering, or a furnisher system migration. Furnisher should identify which tradeline is current and request removal of the duplicate.

guidance.title: Incorrect credit limit / high balance
guidance.guidance: Consumer disputes the reported credit limit or high-balance figure, which affects credit utilization calculations. Often the limit was changed (increased or decreased) but the change wasn't reflected in the furnisher's next report. Furnisher should confirm the current limit on file.

rationale: Confident classification, low-risk reason code, furnisher in good standing.

guidance.title: Suspected identity theft / fraud
guidance.guidance: Consumer states the account was opened fraudulently and not by them. This is treated as higher-risk and time-sensitive; it typically involves fraud-alert or identity-theft procedures beyond a standard reinvestigation, and is generally routed for extra verification rather than auto-processed.
